key_insight: A Gaussian surface bump substantially accelerates vortex-induced boundary-layer transition while preserving the spatio-temporal wave front that signals nonmodal response.
engineering_relevance: Predicting transition under combined surface roughness and free-stream vortices requires accounting for rapid growth of three-dimensional flow structures.
method: Perform 2D and 3D DNS of the incompressible Navier–Stokes equations over a semi-infinite flat plate.
Combine a convecting vortex of fixed strength and sign with a Gaussian surface bump.
Analyze instantaneous flow features, vorticity dynamics, and nonlinear receptivity.
evidence_signal: The simulations identify four stages: roughness-generated disturbances, spatio-temporal amplification, wave-front emergence with unsteady separation bubbles, and bubble merging into turbulent spots.
watch_item: The findings concern a specific Gaussian bump and deterministic vortex forcing; 2D simulations alone cannot accurately capture the roughness-driven evolution toward three-dimensionality.
paper_title: Direct Numerical Simulation of Vortex-Induced Instability Over a Semi-Infinite Flat Plate with Discrete Roughness
